title: campus-half landing floor uses a hardcoded literal 10 instead of the derived per-entry ask
evidence:
testing.expectf(t, campus_window_spawns >= 10*WINDOW*95/100,
		"the campus half must land: in-window campus spawns %d < %d (10/tick × WINDOW × 0.95)", campus_window_spawns, 10*WINDOW*95/100)

EXPECTED := i64(stream_entries) * i64(surge.multiplier) * i64(WINDOW) // 2×1×10×WINDOW = 20×WINDOW
detail: The honest ask (EXPECTED) is derived from the catalog by summing streaming entry volumes, but the campus-half floor hardcodes 10 (= campus volume 1 × multiplier 10). A re-tune of campus volume or the multiplier silently drifts this pin while EXPECTED tracks.
recommended_fix: Derive the campus ask from its own entry (campus volume × surge.multiplier × WINDOW × 95/100), mirroring the stream_entries derivation, instead of the literal 10.

title: fold-check does not detect integer overflow in the hex parse (wraps with ok=true)
detail: strconv.parse_uint does not flag overflow: a >16-hex-digit input wraps to a truncated u64 with ok=true, so the !okh guard never fires. The splice then fails with exit 1 ("differs BEYOND the catalog_hash fold") instead of the intended exit-2 usage error.
recommended_fix: Reject hex strings longer than 16 digits (or detect the overflow) before splicing, and report usage (exit 2) rather than a misleading fold FAIL.
